subject: Request: Onward-transfer permission request for DataStream Analytics (EchoHealth)
messages:
From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@echohealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: EchoHealth Security Team <security@echohealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Onward-transfer permission request: DataStream Analytics

Hi Mina,

Quick note from EchoHealth security/legal — we're running a transfer review for a new analytics partner, DataStream Analytics, who will process de-identified patient telemetry derived from Redwood-powered features for our outcomes research pipeline. EchoHealth's procurement team flagged Redwood as a current subprocessor and asked us to request explicit written permission for this onward transfer under section 6 of our DPA.

Can you confirm:
- Whether DataStream is already listed on Redwood's subprocessor roster (we couldn't find them in last month's export).
- If not, whether Redwood can provide: a SOC 2 Type II report, the standard subprocessor addendum (or confirmation you will sign our DPA amendment), and a short dataflow diagram showing what identifiers (if any) will be shared.

Because EchoHealth handles PHI, we also need a statement about whether DataStream will receive any raw identifiers or only pseudonymized tokens. We need this to close our internal HIPAA review.

Attached: EchoHealth request form (pdf). Please let us know a target date for written consent — our legal team is hoping to close this by COB 2026-02-17.

Thanks,
Sophie Lang
Security & Privacy, EchoHealth

Attachments: echohealth_request_20260210.pdf (form)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@echohealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Onward-transfer permission request: DataStream Analytics

Thanks Sophie — looping in Legal (Lauren), Security (Markus) and Sales (Priyom) so we can get you a consolidated response. I don't want to commit anything until we confirm vendor status and controls.

Action plan from our side:
- Markus: can you check if DataStream appears on our latest subprocessor roster and whether we have a SOC 2 or SIG pack from them?
- Lauren: can you advise what language we need in a DPA amendment to provide the written consent request?
- Priyom: please monitor the EchoHealth procurement timeline; they asked for COB 2026-02-17.

We'll aim to respond with a formal position and any required attachments by EOD Friday (2026-02-13).

— Mina
Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Sent from my laptop.

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Onward-transfer permission request: DataStream Analytics

I've pulled our records. DataStream Analytics is not on the published subprocessor roster (last roster published 2026-01-03). We do have a recent security attachment from DataStream in our intake system (datastream_security_attachment_v1.pdf) but it's an initial questionnaire (no SOC 2).

From a security perspective, red flags / requirements we should confirm before granting written consent:
- SOC 2 Type II or independent SIG/CAIQ; if not available, we need compensating controls and an evidence timeline.
- Contractual requirement: no retention of raw PHI or direct identifiers. Only tokenized/pseudonymized streams permitted.
- Technical: data-at-rest encryption in their environment, key management details, and ephemeral access for ML inference.

If EchoHealth is treating the data as PHI, we should treat this as a high-bar request — recommend requiring a signed DPA amendment and either a SOC 2 Type II or an attestation + a short on-site/remote assessment window before approval.

I can draft a short security addendum to attach to the DPA that enumerates those conditions. Marking this as high priority.

— Markus
Head of Security Assessment

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Onward-transfer permission request: DataStream Analytics

Agree with Markus. For EchoHealth we should provide conditional written consent only after:
1) EchoHealth receives either a signed DPA amendment that includes DataStream as a subprocessor (we can countersign EchoHealth's amendment) OR a Redwood-signed subprocessor addendum naming DataStream;
2) DataStream provides either SOC 2 Type II report or completes our SIG/CAIQ with evidence (and we validate the answers);
3) We receive a clear dataflow diagram and confirmation that no direct identifiers will be shared (or, if identifiers are required, that DataStream will be a BA and sign appropriate HIPAA BAAs).

Draft language for EchoHealth (suggested reply):
"Redwood can provide written permission for DataStream Analytics to process the specified data subject to the execution of a DPA amendment naming DataStream as a subprocessor, and Redwood's receipt of DataStream's SOC 2 Type II report or completed SIG/CAIQ with validated evidence. Prior to any transfer, DataStream must confirm in writing that they will not retain any direct patient identifiers and will implement the technical safeguards described in the attached security addendum."

I'll prepare a countersignable amendment and a short security addendum we can attach. Priyom, if we want to offer EchoHealth an expedited review/temporary approval for a limited POC window, let's scope the timebox and the guards.

— Lauren
Senior Counsel

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 13:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Onward-transfer permission request: DataStream Analytics

EchoHealth is an existing customer and this is a time-sensitive procurement milestone. From a relationship perspective, offering a one-week expedited review that results in "conditional written consent" (i.e., consent that is explicitly conditional on receiving the DPA amendment + SOC 2 / SIG evidence within 30 days) might be acceptable. We could tie any POC activity to a short-term exception (max 14 days) and require that DataStream's access be read-only and only to pseudonymized streams.

If Legal and Security are comfortable with the controls and the language, I support moving on the expedited route to avoid blocking their procurement.

— Priyom
Account Executive

From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@echohealth.com>

Best,
Sophie

Sophie — thank you for the materials and the timeline. Per the internal review above, Redwood can provide the following conditional written consent for EchoHealth's procurement record:

"Redwood Inference provides conditional written consent for DataStream Analytics to process the pseudonymized telemetry dataset derived from EchoHealth services, subject to the following conditions: (1) execution of a DPA amendment naming DataStream Analytics as a subprocessor and countersigned by Redwood; (2) Redwood's receipt of a SOC 2 Type II report from DataStream, or a completed SIG/CAIQ with validated evidence and a remediation plan for any gaps, within 30 days of the DPA amendment execution; (3) DataStream's written confirmation that it will not receive or retain direct patient identifiers and will implement the technical safeguards described in Redwood's security addendum (encryption at rest, access controls, and key management); and (4) any short-term POC access (if requested) will be limited to pseudonymized read-only streams and will be timeboxed to a maximum of 14 days pending full evidence.

Provided the above conditions are met within the stated timelines, Redwood will confirm final consent in writing. This conditional consent is intended for procurement/audit purposes and does not constitute a waiver of Redwood's contractual rights under its DPA.

Please let us know if EchoHealth needs this on Redwood letterhead or as a countersigned DPA amendment — Lauren's team can produce the countersignable doc and Markus will attach the security addendum.

— Mina Haddad
Product Ops, Redwood Inference
